title: Benchmark telemetry harness
description: Objective: emit the machine-readable run, cost-class, timing, effort, settings, evidence-receipt, and reproducibility records required by the pinned benchmark. Deliverable: benchmark harness infrastructure without confirmatory corpus bytes. NOT in scope: competitor scoring or claim decisions. Hard dependencies: stable daemon/provider/control-room instrumentation. Owned paths: packages/benchmark/** excluding confirmatory corpus and campaign outputs. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/benchmark test.
definitionOfDone: Every required measurement has exact source/basis or explicit UNKNOWN; UNKNOWN is never zero or imputed across arms.
Run records bind model/profile/runtime/settings/source/evidence identities and all timing split points.
Harness self-tests cover censoring, cost bases, fixtures, concurrency, and receipt tamper.
taskRails: Claims follow the benchmark permit-list; missing, partial, cross-basis, or unverifiable evidence is UNKNOWN, never PASS.
No confirmatory corpus is generated or viewed until the implementation commit is frozen exactly as specified.
GO_QUIESCE and GO_ACTIVATE are separate human decisions. Keep evidence exact, reproducible, and scoped to one source commit.

Reproduce that and quote it. It is the reason this task's own verification command has been unfalsifiable across three prior audits.
Create `packages/benchmark/package.json` and `packages/benchmark/tsconfig.json`, copying the shape of an existing workspace package rather than inventing one — `packages/coordination/package.json` is the template: `{name, version 0.0.0, private true, type module, exports {".": "./src/index.ts"}, scripts: {typecheck: "tsc --project tsconfig.json", test: "vitest run --root ../.. packages/benchmark/src"}}`, and its tsconfig extends `../../tsconfig.base.json` with `rootDir: "src"`, its own `tsBuildInfoFile`, and `types: ["node"]`. DEPENDENCIES: keep them minimal and justified. This package projects evidence; it does not read a store. Do NOT add `@moe/store` or reach for apps/daemon — a package cannot import from an app, which is the constraint step 2 is built around.

implementationPlan.description:
SETTLE THE INPUT BOUNDARY, which is the design question this task has never answered. The records the harness projects are `ProviderRunRecord`s declared at `apps/daemon/src/telemetry/provider-run-contracts.ts:94`. A PACKAGE CANNOT IMPORT FROM AN APP, so the harness cannot take that type by reference.
THE ANSWER: the harness accepts BOUNDED PLAIN DATA and validates SHAPE ONLY. It pins `recordVersion` against `PROVIDER_RUN_RECORD_VERSION` (`"moe-provider-run-record/1"`, contracts.ts:57) as a literal it declares itself, and refuses anything else. That literal is the seam — when the record schema moves, this package reddens instead of silently projecting a shape it no longer understands.
AND THE LINE IT MUST NOT CROSS: the harness PROJECTS, it never DECIDES. It re-derives no fact the codec already established, recomputes no digest, and mints no measurement. Shape validation answers "is this the schema I project?" and nothing more. A second validator that re-judged the evidence would be a competing authority over records the daemon's codec already sealed — exactly what the codec's own comment ("the codec is the only authority on what is a record") forecloses.
Write that boundary into the package's index header, with the version literal and the reason, so the next reader can tell projection from adjudication at a glance.
CONSUMER EDGE (Clause 1): this package is infrastructure and lands with a named consumer rather than a call site — task-3a34adcabd03489e84f8dfbec913633a (corpus freeze), which the governor's cascade records as unblocking as this lands, followed by task-8af4562ff1ae41b28876aaee63f05ea3 (benchmark campaign). Record both ids in the completion.
implementationPlan.note:

THE BOUNDARY: the harness accepts BOUNDED PLAIN DATA and validates SHAPE ONLY. `ProviderRunRecord` is declared at apps/daemon/src/telemetry/provider-run-contracts.ts:94 and a package cannot import from an app, so the type cannot be taken by reference. Records arrive already decoded and already sealed by the daemon's codec.

THE VERSION SEAM: `PROJECTED_RECORD_VERSION = "moe-provider-run-record/1"` declared as its own literal in benchmark-record-contracts.ts, pinned against the daemon's PROVIDER_RUN_RECORD_VERSION (contracts.ts:57). Admission will refuse every other value. Drill 6 will prove the seam catches a schema move.

THE LINE IT MUST NOT CROSS, written into the index header verbatim: this package PROJECTS, it never DECIDES. No re-derivation, no digest recomputation, no minted measurement, no scoring, no ranking, no claim decisions, no corpus bytes. Shape validation answers "is this the schema I project?" and nothing more; the codec's own comment ("the codec is the only authority on what is a record", activation-run-commit.ts:236) forecloses a second adjudicator.

I MEASURED THE REAL EMISSION PATH rather than trusting the description. `composeProviderRunRecord` (activation-run-commit.ts:185-219) freezes exactly 20 keys; `recordDigest` is composed as `""` and the CODEC overwrites it after digesting the canonical record with that field excluded. So the committed record the harness reads carries a codec-filled digest — the harness carries it verbatim and recomputes nothing, which is also why drill 6 targets the version literal rather than the digest (a caller-supplied-digest drill here would be an equivalent mutant, exactly as task-d3239529's handoff recorded).

SHAPES VERIFIED ON DISK, not assumed — every field of the mirror was read from its producing file:
- ProviderRunRef, ProviderQuantity, ProviderText, ProviderFactUnknown, ProviderCountCoverage — runner/providers/telemetry/provider-telemetry-contracts.ts:132-147, :54-56
- ClaudeTelemetryLaunchFacts (13 fields), ClaudeDeclaredSelection, ClaudeTelemetryConcurrency — runner/providers/telemetry/claude-telemetry-launch.ts:40-64
- ClaudeObservedModel, ClaudeTokenObservations, ClaudeStepObservations — runner/providers/telemetry/claude-result-telemetry.ts:83-96
- ClaudeLaunchSelection (10 fields; reasoningEffort and profileRevisionId live HERE and nowhere else) — runner/providers/claude/claude-launch-selection.ts:93-104
- ClockObservation — scheduler/authority/authority-kernel.ts:107-111
- NormalizedMeasurement, PricebookBinding, LayeredIssue — scheduler/budget/budget-measurement.ts:40-57
- UsageMeasurementRecord — scheduler/budget/budget-contract.ts:76-82

TWO DESIGN CALLS I MADE EXPLICIT IN THE FILE HEADER, because both look wrong at a glance:
1. Re-declaring shapes here is the OPPOSITE of the daemon's rule ("every record field is typed from its producing package's public root"). That rule exists because the daemon WRITES durable bytes and an unnoticed producer drift is uncorrectable. This package only READS bytes that are already durable; a drift it missed would corrupt nothing, it would merely project a stale shape — which is precisely what the version literal refuses.
2. Closed vocabularies (terminal, infrastructure, coverage, truthClass, refusal codes) are typed `string`, not re-listed. Re-listing their members would create a second vocabulary for one condition and entitle this package to an opinion about which members are valid — an opinion the codec already formed. They are carried through verbatim and adjudicated not at all.

Also added PROJECTED_RECORD_KEYS as a frozen iterable array of the 19 top-level keys, so step 4's absent-field sweep can drive one missing key per case at RUNTIME. A type cannot be walked to generate cases; that is why the array exists rather than a keyof.

CONSUMER EDGE (Clause 1), named as required for infrastructure: task-3a34adcabd03489e84f8dfbec913633a (corpus freeze) first, then task-8af4562ff1ae41b28876aaee63f05ea3 (benchmark campaign).

Sizes by grep -c '': benchmark-record-contracts.ts 209, index.ts 45. Both under 250. One-line .js bridge added for the contracts module per the repo convention (index.ts is the entry and takes no bridge, matching packages/coordination).

implementationPlan.description:
FREEZE THE UNKNOWN VOCABULARY — the open question three architects have deferred. The harness needs its own closed reason-code and layer lists for the cases where it cannot project a row, and they must be frozen arrays a test can ITERATE, not a type: a test cannot iterate a type, and a sweep needs every member at runtime. Follow the repo's established shape — `Object.freeze([...] as const)` plus a derived union type, as `COORDINATION_CODES`/`COORDINATION_LAYERS` and `PROVIDER_TELEMETRY_LAYERS` do.
SCOPE IT TIGHTLY: codes for what the HARNESS cannot project — an unrecognised record version, a record whose required field is absent, a row whose basis is missing. NOT codes for what the run itself did; those already exist on the record as `terminal`, `infrastructure`, `upstreamRefusal` and `usageRefusals`, and duplicating them here would create a second vocabulary for one condition.
NO CAMPAIGN SCORING, NO CLAIM DECISIONS. This vocabulary describes projection failures. A code that means "this arm scored worse" or "this claim is unproven" belongs to the campaign task, not here — that boundary is why this task is infrastructure-only.
Assert the closed lists: every member reachable, a positive case count on any sweep over them, and no member declared without a producer. A code no layer can emit cannot fail closed — the same defect QA rejected on task-6cbff010 for exactly this reason.

FIVE CODES, scoped to projection failures only:
  BENCHMARK_RECORD_FIELD_ABSENT, BENCHMARK_RECORD_FIELD_MALFORMED,
  BENCHMARK_RECORD_NOT_PLAIN_DATA, BENCHMARK_RECORD_VERSION_UNRECOGNISED,
  BENCHMARK_ROW_BASIS_ABSENT
FOUR LAYERS, ordered as they answer:
  BENCHMARK_INPUT, BENCHMARK_VERSION, BENCHMARK_SHAPE, BENCHMARK_ROW

THE THREE EXCLUSIONS ARE WRITTEN INTO THE MODULE HEADER, since each is a code someone will later be tempted to add:
1. NOT what the run did — terminal/infrastructure/upstreamRefusal/usageRefusals already say that in the runner's and scheduler's own vocabularies. A "provider refused" code here would be a second vocabulary for one condition.
2. NOT what a campaign concluded — no "scored worse", no "claim unproven". That is task-8af4562f's, and a projector holding a verdict decides the claim it exists to measure.
3. NOT a replacement for UNKNOWN — an unobserved reading is UNKNOWN on the row carrying the PRODUCING authority's code and layer, not a refusal here. These five fire only when the harness cannot emit the row at all. This distinction is the one most likely to be eroded later.

PRODUCER MAP, one layer per code, no overlap (a code no layer can emit cannot fail closed — the defect QA rejected on task-6cbff010):
  BENCHMARK_INPUT   -> NOT_PLAIN_DATA          (input is not a plain object at all)
  BENCHMARK_VERSION -> VERSION_UNRECOGNISED    (runs before shape: an unrecognised schema means the harness cannot know which fields to expect)
  BENCHMARK_SHAPE   -> FIELD_ABSENT, FIELD_MALFORMED (two codes, one layer, but DISTINCT codes so an assertion can still tell which answered)
  BENCHMARK_ROW     -> ROW_BASIS_ABSENT        (admission accepts `usage` as an array in bulk; a row that is not a readable measurement is refused here)
Every layer has at least one producer and every code exactly one producing site. Step 4 turns this map into an executable producer-coverage sweep against the real admission/projection surface; step 5 makes it green. It could not be asserted in this step without the production surface existing, and asserting it against a test helper would be the "property asserted against a reimplementation" defect the epic rail names.

SWEEP VACUITY GUARDED, per the rail that a sweep producing zero cases passes silently: every sweeping test counts its generated cases and asserts both the exact expected count AND `toBeGreaterThan(0)`. The refusal-minting sweep drives all 5 codes x 4 layers = 20 pairings and asserts swept === 20.

Other assertions chosen to be mutation-resistant rather than structural theatre: both lists frozen and duplicate-free; codes asserted against a hand-written literal list (so a silent addition reddens rather than being absorbed); messages exhaustive in BOTH directions (`Object.keys(MESSAGES).sort()` equals the code list, so neither an unmessaged code nor an orphan message survives); messages mutually DISTINCT (a copy-paste onto a second code would make the two indistinguishable in durable bytes); and no message contains its own code or any of `$ { }` — pinning the no-echo rule the runner's own PROVIDER_TELEMETRY_MESSAGES states, so a failure path cannot start quoting record content.

benchmarkProjectionRefusal is the single mint point, returning a frozen flat {ok:false, code, layer, message}; a flat Object.freeze is a complete freeze here, no deepFreeze needed. Shape mirrors ProviderTelemetryRefusal but the vocabulary is disjoint by construction — that is what keeps the three refusal sources unflattenable.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED — the non-merge rules, which are the harness's entire substance. Every one of these is a rule the RECORD's own comments already state; the harness must not undo them in projection. Write them before the projector exists.
(a) DECLARED IS NOT OBSERVED. `declared` carries what was asked for (selected model, reasoning effort, profile revision); `observedModel` carries what the provider's bytes said. The record comment says merging them "destroys the only evidence that the provider ran the model it was asked to run". Assert the projection keeps them as separate fields and that an absent `observedModel` is NOT filled from `declared` — the old handoffs' "do not substitute runtime/profile IDs for model snapshot or reasoning effort" is exactly this.
(b) TWO CLOCKS, NOT RECONCILED. `launch.startedAt`/`completedAt` are the LAUNCHER's wall stamps; `observedStart`/`observedEnd` are the daemon's own `ClockObservation`s. The comment says they are "two observers, deliberately not reconciled". Assert the projection reports both and derives no single timing from a mix of them.
(c) A DURATION NEEDS ONE BOOT. A `ClockObservation` binds wall seconds, boot identity and monotonic reading together, because "a duration derived from a pair without `bootId` is unfalsifiable". Assert the harness emits a duration ONLY when both observations share a `bootId`, and UNKNOWN otherwise — with a case where the boot ids differ.
(d) NULL IS NOT ZERO. "`null` is an unobserved reading and never a zero." Assert no null observation, absent token count or missing usage row is ever rendered as 0, and that a `ProviderCountCoverage` short of complete is carried through rather than dropped.
(e) A BINDING IS NOT A COST. Usage rows carry `pricebookBinding`, and "a derived list price stays a binding and never becomes an actual-cost claim". Assert the cost-class column reports the binding and never presents a derived price as an actual cost.
(f) NO IMPUTATION ACROSS ARMS. Assert one record's UNKNOWN is never filled from another record's value — drive two records where one is complete and one is not, and assert the incomplete one stays incomplete.
Every refusal case pins the exact frozen code AND layer from step 3. Assert a positive generated-case count on any sweep.

RULES WRITTEN, one test per rule, each pinned to a value a one-character change would move.

(a) DECLARED IS NOT OBSERVED — 5 tests. The key one drives a record whose `declared` is FULLY READABLE while `observedModel.modelId` is unknown, because that is the shape where substitution looks like a helpful default. Asserts observedModelId equals {known:false, basis:PRODUCER_DECLARED_UNKNOWN, code:TELEMETRY_MODEL_ABSENT, layer:TELEMETRY_RESULT} and, separately, that JSON.stringify(modelEvidence) does not contain "claude-opus-5" — so drill 1 reddens on both the shape and the leaked value. Extended the rule to the SAME trap on concurrency, which the runner's own contract flags: `achieved` is unsupported by construction and `declaredCeiling` is a REQUEST, so achievedConcurrency must stay UNKNOWN with its producer code even though a 4 is sitting right next to it. Also asserts effort/profileRevisionId come from `declared` alone and go SELECTION_UNREADABLE when it is not readable — never substituted from a digest.

(b) TWO CLOCKS — 4 tests. Launcher pair and daemon pair asserted as separate columns, each verbatim. The duration is pinned to 12 (the monotonic delta) where the wall delta is 30 and the launcher stamps are hours away, so drill 2's mixed-observer derivation cannot land on the right number by luck. Plus an exact-key-set assertion on `timing` so no reconciled column can be added silently.

(c) A DURATION NEEDS ONE BOOT — 3 tests. The mismatch fixture differs from the good one in bootId AND NOTHING ELSE, and the test asserts daemonStart.known and daemonEnd.known are both true BEFORE asserting the duration is unknown. That is what makes drill 3 redden on the boot mismatch specifically rather than on a missing field. A sibling test pins the two UNKNOWN reasons apart: absent observation is basis OBSERVATION_ABSENT, boot mismatch is BOOT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH. Both produce an unknown, so without distinct bases the rule would be untestable.

(d) NULL IS NOT ZERO — 4 tests. A whole-projection walk asserts the unobserved record serialises without any '"value":0', PAIRED WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL asserting the complete record's projection does contain '"value":' — without that control the walk would pass on an empty object. Plus: a null measurement quantity becomes QUANTITY_ABSENT; all 6 unobserved count cells carry the producing authority's own code; and coverage short of complete (PARTIAL, UNKNOWN) is carried through rather than dropped.

(e) A BINDING IS NOT A COST — 4 tests. The binding is asserted verbatim, the cost row's EXACT key set is pinned (so drill 5's derived-price field reddens on the key set), and the row is asserted not to contain "6000" — quantity 4 x 1500 micros, a number that appears nowhere in the record, so a list price presented as an actual cost cannot blend in. The unbound row must read NO_BINDING with no price key at all, not a zero cost.

(f) NO IMPUTATION ACROSS ARMS — 3 tests. Projects the complete arm, then the incomplete one, and asserts the incomplete one's unknowns survive and that its serialisation does not contain the complete arm's observed model id. A second test projects the incomplete arm both after the complete one and alone, and deep-equals the two — which catches memoisation or module state, not just a copy inside one call.

PRODUCER COVERAGE, the step-3 debt now executable: a PRODUCERS table drives one real input per frozen code, asserts the exact code AND layer for each, then asserts the produced code set equals BENCHMARK_PROJECTION_CODES and the produced layer set equals BENCHMARK_PROJECTION_LAYERS — in BOTH directions, so neither an unproducible member nor an unlisted producer survives. Every malformed and row-level fixture is built from the COMPLETE record so it is valid at the earlier layers and actually reaches the guard under test; otherwise an earlier guard would answer and the assertion would quietly detach.

SWEEP VACUITY: every sweeping test counts its cases and asserts both the exact count and >0. The absent-field sweep additionally asserts swept === 18 as a literal alongside PROJECTED_RECORD_KEYS.length - 1, so a shrunken key list cannot silently shrink the sweep.

CENSORING (DoD self-test item): a sweep asserts no refusal message contains "claude-opus-5", "run-1" or the record digest.

RECEIPT TAMPER (DoD self-test item): the harness reports a tampered recordDigest VERBATIM and still projects. That is the correct behaviour, not a gap — recomputing would be a second, drifting opinion about bytes the codec already sealed, and refusing would make the harness a validator. The test pins projection-not-adjudication.

implementationPlan.description:
IMPLEMENT THE PROJECTION. Create the projector under `packages/benchmark/src/` — one module per concern if it would otherwise exceed 250 physical lines, measured with `grep -c ''` (PowerShell `Measure-Object -Line` undercounts). It turns a validated record into the harness's row set: run identity, cost class, timing, effort, settings, evidence receipt, reproducibility.
Each column carries its own provenance and its own UNKNOWN. Run identity comes from `providerRunRef` verbatim — "never three hand-rolled ids". Effort and settings come from `declared`, model evidence from `observedModel`, and the two stay separate columns. Timing carries the launcher pair and the daemon pair separately, with a derived duration only under a shared `bootId`. Cost class reports each usage row's `pricebookBinding` alongside its measurement, never a computed total presented as actual. Evidence receipt carries `stdoutReceiptDigest`/`stderrReceiptDigest` and `recordDigest` verbatim. Reproducibility carries `launch`'s runtime and profile digests verbatim.
Refusals stay disjoint exactly as the record keeps them: `usageRefusals` are the scheduler's layered issues, `upstreamRefusal` is the provider seam's, and the harness's own frozen codes cover only what IT could not project. Three sources, never flattened — flattening would make a scheduler issue indistinguishable from a provider refusal, which is the same defect the record's own comment guards against.
NO CORPUS BYTES, NO SCORING, NO CLAIM DECISIONS. This module reads one record and emits its rows. Comparing arms, ranking them, or deciding a claim belongs to the campaign task.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. `pnpm --filter @moe/benchmark test` -> `Test Files 4 passed (4)` / `Tests 48 passed (48)`, EXIT=0. `pnpm --filter @moe/benchmark typecheck` EXIT=0, run as its own leg.

FOUR MODULES, split by concern to stay well under the per-file cap:
- benchmark-record-admission.ts (130) — the four guards, in the order they answer.
- benchmark-projection-cells.ts (62) — the four ways a cell comes into existence, and no fifth.
- benchmark-cost-projection.ts (87) — cost rows and counts.
- benchmark-run-projection.ts (213) — the projector and the column types.

THE ONE DESIGN DECISION WORTH FLAGGING: every UNKNOWN in this harness is constructed in benchmark-projection-cells.ts and nowhere else. That concentration is deliberate — the failure this package exists to prevent is a null quietly becoming a 0, and a rule enforced in one function is a rule a single drill can falsify. Scattering the same logic across four modules would make drill 4 prove only that one of four sites was correct.

GUARD ORDER, each layer answering a strictly earlier question: INPUT (plain record at all) -> VERSION (a revision I read) -> SHAPE (fields present, then fields of the projected kind) -> ROW (each usage row readable). Version before shape is load-bearing: an unrecognised schema means the harness cannot know which fields to expect, so a field complaint would be noise about a shape it was never entitled to assume. `recordVersion` is deliberately ABSENT from the shape table so a shape complaint can never answer for a schema move — that is what keeps drill 6 landing on the version guard.

Admission is shape-only. It recomputes no digest, checks no digest, re-derives no identity and forms no view on whether a value is plausible. The single `as` cast on the success arm is the documented boundary of the module. `isPlainRecord` rejects arrays, functions and class instances by prototype check: the input is meant to be decoded durable data, and anything carrying behaviour did not come from the store.

PROJECTION RULES AS IMPLEMENTED:
- runIdentity is `providerRunRef` whole — never three hand-rolled ids.
- effort/settings read `declared` only; modelEvidence reads `observedModel` only. There is no code path from one to the other. When `declared` is unreadable the three effort cells go UNKNOWN under SELECTION_UNREADABLE carrying the producer's own code, rather than borrowing the runtime or profile digests that sit one field away.
- Concurrency keeps the same separation: `declaredCeiling` is a request, `achieved` stays UNKNOWN with TELEMETRY_ACHIEVED_CONCURRENCY_UNSUPPORTED. The pinned provider schema carries no achieved-concurrency field, so there is no member of the runner's own vocabulary that would let it be filled from the ceiling.
- Timing carries both observers side by side. The single derived number, daemonMonotonicDuration, comes from the daemon's monotonic pair alone and only under a shared bootId. The wall seconds sitting right there are deliberately NOT a fallback — falling back would answer with a different observer's measurement under the same column name, which is precisely the silent reconciliation the record's contract forbids.
- Cost rows contain no multiplication and no field a total could be written into. quantity, pricebookBinding and costBasis are three separate things; a consumer that wants a price computes it and owns the claim.
- Evidence receipts and the seven reproducibility digests are carried verbatim; a null digest becomes UNKNOWN, never an empty string.

REFUSAL SOURCES — I corrected my own step-4 test here rather than build a field to satisfy it. I had drafted `refusals.projection` as a third column, but on the success path it is empty BY CONSTRUCTION: the harness fails closed, so when it cannot project there is no projection to hold a column. An always-empty array would have been a field with no producer — the exact defect this task's rails name. The record's two sources stay as two columns (scheduler, provider) and the third source is the refusal RESULT TYPE, which is structurally impossible to confuse with them. The replacement test asserts that no BENCHMARK_* code appears anywhere in either column, sweeping all five.

I also corrected a second test of my own: the cost-row key-set assertion had "coverage" before "costBasis", which is not the lexicographic order Array.sort produces ("costBasis" < "coverage" because 's' < 'v'). Fixed to the real order — an assertion that cannot hold is not a guard.

TWO VOCABULARIES ADDED WITH THEIR PRODUCER SWEEPS, since both were introduced during implementation and neither may ship undeclared:
- BENCHMARK_UNKNOWN_BASES — a recursive walk collects every `basis` a real projection emitted across two records and asserts the produced set EQUALS the frozen list, both directions. HOLE 1 — NON-FINITE READINGS. `typeof x === "number"` accepts NaN and the infinities. A NaN monotonic reading would have passed admission and flowed into the one place this package subtracts, publishing `{known:true, value:NaN}` — a value present in no record, wearing the authority of an observation. That is UNKNOWN gaining authority by the back door, which epic rail 4 forbids. Admission now requires `Number.isFinite` on both observation readings, on a measurement quantity, and on a row sequence. This is a SHAPE question, not adjudication: a non-finite reading is not a reading. No new codes were needed — a bad observation is FIELD_MALFORMED@BENCHMARK_SHAPE and a bad row is ROW_BASIS_ABSENT@BENCHMARK_ROW, both existing producers.

The fixtures are now deeply frozen. This is also the more faithful shape: `composeProviderRunRecord` freezes the record it commits, so a frozen fixture is what a real reader receives. Spreading to build variants is unaffected, and a test asserts that explicitly.
  DRILL 8: removed `deepFreeze` from `completeRunRecordFixture`. RED on "refuses in-place mutation of a fixture at every depth" — `expected false to be true`. Guard proven.

- INPUTS: null/undefined/string/number/boolean/array/function all refused at BENCHMARK_INPUT. Prototype-pollution shapes are refused by the explicit `Object.getPrototypeOf` check, and presence uses `Object.hasOwn` rather than `in`, so an inherited key cannot satisfy a required field. planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) Have the harness read the store directly and decode committed records itself. REJECTED: it would need `@moe/store` plus the daemon's codec, and a package cannot import from an app. It would also duplicate decode authority the codec already owns.

2) Move `ProviderRunRecord` into a package so the harness can import it. REJECTED as out of scope and a foreign-file edit: contracts.ts belongs to the telemetry slice, and relocating a sealed record type to satisfy a consumer inverts the dependency the codec's authority rests on.

3) Put the harness in apps/daemon instead of creating the package. REJECTED: the task's own verification names `pnpm --filter @moe/benchmark test`, and the vacuous-gate hazard is only closed by making that filter resolve. Leaving the package absent preserves the exact unfalsifiable gate three audits flagged.

4) Have the harness re-validate the evidence it projects. REJECTED: that is a competing authority over sealed records. Shape-and-version validation answers "is this the schema I project?"; anything further adjudicates.

5) Reconcile the launcher and daemon clock pairs into one timing. REJECTED by the record's own comment — reconciling means overwriting one with the other, and the durable bytes would then no longer say which clock was read. Report both; derive only under a shared bootId.

6) Default an absent `observedModel` from `declared` so every row has a model. REJECTED and drilled: it destroys the only evidence that the provider ran what it was asked to run. This is the most plausible-looking wrong move in the whole task, which is why drill 1 targets it.

7) Include campaign scoring or claim decisions so the harness is "useful". REJECTED: infrastructure only. Scoring belongs to task-8af4562f, corpus to task-3a34adca, and mixing them is how a harness starts deciding claims it was built to measure.

8) Add the frozen vocabulary later, once failures are known. REJECTED: it is the open question three architects deferred, and a code added after the fact tends to be added without a producer — the exact defect QA rejected on task-6cbff010.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD 3e52753. I ran this task's Clause-2 audit earlier and filed the two prerequisites; both have landed, so the harness now has real emitted records to project.

THE WIRE IS CLOSED. All three greps that returned ZERO at my audit now return production hits: `activation-telemetry-launch.ts:95-96` calls `launchClaudeWithTelemetry`; `activation-run-commit.ts:51,133` calls `buildProviderRunRecord`; `activation-run-commit.ts:242` calls `commitProviderRunRecord`. Production emits and durably commits provider-run telemetry.

THE VACUOUS GATE IS STILL LIVE AND REPRODUCES EXACTLY: `pnpm --filter @moe/benchmark test` prints `No projects matched the filters in "D:\projexts\moe-next"` and EXITS 0. `packages/benchmark` is absent. This is why the task's own verification has been unfalsifiable across three audits, and why package creation plus a NONZERO count line is step 1 rather than an afterthought.

THE INPUT-BOUNDARY PROBLEM, which no prior pass named. `ProviderRunRecord` is declared at `apps/daemon/src/telemetry/provider-run-contracts.ts:94`. A PACKAGE CANNOT IMPORT FROM AN APP, so `packages/benchmark` cannot take that type by reference. The resolution is bounded plain data plus a self-declared `recordVersion` literal pinned against `PROVIDER_RUN_RECORD_VERSION` = "moe-provider-run-record/1" (contracts.ts:57), with SHAPE validation only — the harness projects, it never adjudicates. Anything more would be a second authority over records the daemon codec already sealed, and the codec's own comment says it "is the only authority on what is a record".

THE RECORD PRE-ANSWERS MOST OF THE HARNESS DESIGN. Its field comments state rules the projection must not undo, and every one matches a pitfall the prior handoffs recorded independently:
- `declared` (asked for) vs `observedModel` (what the bytes said): "Never defaulted from `declared`: a selection is not an observation, and merging them destroys the only evidence that the provider ran the model it was asked to run." That IS "do not substitute runtime/profile IDs for model snapshot or effort".
- `observedStart`/`observedEnd` are `ClockObservation | null`, binding wall seconds + bootId + monotonic together, because "a duration derived from a pair without `bootId` is unfalsifiable" — and they are "DISTINCT FROM `launch.startedAt`/`completedAt`", "two observers, deliberately not reconciled". That IS "do not accept caller-supplied timing pairs in place of production observations".
- "`null` is an unobserved reading and never a zero." That IS "UNKNOWN must never be rendered as zero".
- `usage` rows carry `pricebookBinding`: "A derived list price stays a binding and never becomes an actual-cost claim."
- `tokens`/`steps` carry their own `ProviderCountCoverage`; `usageRefusals` (scheduler, layered) and `upstreamRefusal` (provider seam) are disjoint by construction.

PACKAGE SCAFFOLD, measured from `packages/coordination`: package.json with `type: module`, `exports {".": "./src/index.ts"}`, `typecheck: "tsc --project tsconfig.json"`, `test: "vitest run --root ../.. packages/<name>/src"`; tsconfig extends `../../tsconfig.base.json` with `rootDir: "src"`, its own tsBuildInfoFile, `types: ["node"]`. The `--root ../..` is what makes vitest print a real count line. Workspace glob is `packages/*`, so the package resolves once the manifest exists and the lockfile has its importer.
planningNotes.risks:
1) THE GATE HAS NEVER BEEN REAL. `pnpm --filter @moe/benchmark test` exits 0 on an absent package. Require the `Test Files`/`Tests` count line with a NONZERO M, plus a positive control against a package that certainly has tests. Quote the step-1 baseline beside the final output — that before/after pair is the only closing evidence for a hazard three audits carried.

2) THE LOCKFILE IS AN OWNED PATH. Creating a workspace package requires an install; forgetting to commit `pnpm-lock.yaml` leaves the package unresolvable for everyone else while passing locally.

3) FILLING `observedModel` FROM `declared` LOOKS HELPFUL. It is the substitution three handoffs warned about, and it silently destroys the evidence that the provider ran the model it was asked to run. Drill 1 exists for it.

4) A DURATION ACROSS TWO OBSERVERS, OR ACROSS BOOTS, IS UNFALSIFIABLE. Drills 2 and 3 cover both, and drill 3 must redden on the BOOT MISMATCH specifically — a missing field also yields UNKNOWN, so a red for the wrong reason would leave the rule untested.

5) NULL RENDERED AS ZERO is the classic UNKNOWN-laundering move, and a spreadsheet-shaped output invites it. Drill 4 guards it.

6) A `pricebookBinding` PRESENTED AS AN ACTUAL COST turns a derived list price into a cost claim — the exact thing the record's comment forbids, and the thing a benchmark harness is most tempted to do.

7) THREE DISJOINT REFUSAL SOURCES — scheduler `usageRefusals`, provider `upstreamRefusal`, and the harness's own projection codes. Flattening them makes a scheduler issue indistinguishable from a provider refusal.

8) SCOPE CREEP INTO SCORING. Corpus is task-3a34adca and campaign is task-8af4562f. A harness that ranks arms has started deciding the claim it exists to measure.

9) A CODE WITH NO PRODUCER cannot fail closed — QA rejected task-6cbff010 for exactly that. Every frozen member needs a producer and a code+layer test.

10) SHARED WORKTREE. Re-check `git status --porcelain` before committing, commit by explicit pathspec including the lockfile, verify with `git show --stat`, confirm every drill reverted.

11) CONSUMER EDGE: this is infrastructure, so Clause 1 is satisfied by NAMING the consumer — task-3a34adcabd03489e84f8dfbec913633a then task-8af4562ff1ae41b28876aaee63f05ea3. Record both ids rather than assuming the edge.
